createProjectArguments.description:
# Devpost project draft — release review required

## Project name / tagline

Waylatch — Offline-ready emergency procurement and accountable payments.

Tagline: From field need to verified action.

## Problem and audience

Field responders, volunteer coordinators and nonprofit teams may need to request supplies before reliable connectivity returns. Lost requests and duplicate expense records make later authorization and reconciliation harder. Waylatch preserves the request, carries it between devices and maintains a clear boundary between AI evidence and human financial authority.

## What it does

A field request survives offline reload in IndexedDB. Compact MessagePack QR packets reconstruct it on another device, preserving unknown fields and import provenance. A local MiniLM embedding model compares descriptions alongside exact receipt, amount, incident and time indicators. A human records a disposition and explicitly approves a frozen procurement revision. PayPal Sandbox Orders v2 supplies buyer approval and capture, while authoritative order inspection reconciles the resulting payment. SHA-256-linked events connect record, review, approval and transaction references. Separate incurred-expense claims receive human review without becoming purchase orders.

**Verified prototype status:** offline reload, QR transfer and real local embeddings have executed. The genuine PayPal Sandbox purchase is now complete: order **2W330508JA572391V**, capture **8WY07860808872629**, provider status **COMPLETED**, application state **PAID**, exact **USD 1.00 simulated funds / USD 0.00 real spending**. The actual user reviewed and authorized request **RL-REAL-20261013-201748**, revision **1**, approved checkout as the Sandbox buyer, and separately authorized capture. Seven exported audit events independently validate. [New independent read-only provider GETs](evidence/paypal-independent-verification.json) returned HTTP200/COMPLETED for both order and capture, matching the exact amount/reference and single final capture. See [sanitized provider evidence](evidence/paypal-real-sandbox.json) and [decision/audit provenance](PAYPAL_AUTHENTICATED_CONTINUATION.md). The buyer's mobile loopback return page failed; authoritative provider inspection confirmed approval and capture independently. Payouts transfer and real webhook delivery remain unverified. This is a private draft awaiting publication and legal approval.

## How we built it

React, TypeScript and Vite supply a responsive four-stage command interface. IndexedDB and a production service worker preserve field continuity. Strict Zod validation and bounded MessagePack/CRC32 envelopes treat imports as untrusted. Node 24 / Express and built-in SQLite hold durable review, authorization, reservations and audit events. The official Sandbox REST APIs handle OAuth, Orders v2 creation/details/capture and webhook signature verification. Pinned Apache-2.0 MiniLM ONNX weights run through Transformers.js on local CPU without external inference calls. AI recommendations cannot execute or reject a payment.

## Innovation / impact

The integration makes connectivity loss part of procurement operations: field capture, a disconnected handoff, explainable duplicate review, explicit financial authorization and reconciliation are one continuous product flow. CRCs do not masquerade as authentication, semantic similarity does not masquerade as fraud certainty, and unknown data cannot silently become payment authority.

This is a synthetic prototype for a specific operational problem, not evidence of emergency readiness. Impact requires testing with representative organizations and field workflows before real-world deployment.

## New work and reuse

The original RescueLedger implementation was created during the 2026 submission period and continues as Waylatch without rebuilding or rewriting its history. With owner authorization, it selectively adapts CrisisCodec's codec/reconstruction primitives at commit 8ca845c; request/claim domain, guarded PayPal integration, local semantic review, audit chain and visual product are new work. CrisisCodec UI/domain behavior was not cloned. Exact source adaptation and rights limitations are disclosed in CRISISCODEC_REUSE.md.

## Technology list

PayPal Developer Platform (executed Sandbox OAuth, Orders v2 creation/details, browser buyer approval and capture; webhook verification client implemented and locally tested, real delivery unverified); React; TypeScript; Vite; Node.js 24; Express; SQLite (node:sqlite); IndexedDB/idb; Service Worker API; Zod; MessagePack (@msgpack/msgpack); qrcode; jsQR; Transformers.js; ONNX Runtime CPU; Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Apache-2.0, q8); SHA-256/Web Crypto; Vitest; Playwright; axe-core; Git/GitHub; Python (pinned model asset downloader and video editing/rendering tooling); FFmpeg/FFprobe (silent captioned demo production tools).

No Nebius, paid inference, Tavily critical dependency, credit/lending service or live PayPal mode. Payouts probe support is not a completed reimbursement integration.

## What remains before submission

Approve the concrete release candidate through [RELEASE_APPROVALS.md](RELEASE_APPROVALS.md): source ownership/CrisisCodec public rights, proposed MIT adoption, AMBER branding, public repository, the evidence-backed YouTube demo, participant eligibility/representation, registration/legal terms and final Devpost action. Registration and exact custom form fields are unknown because Devpost read tools returned internal error -32603. No registration, agreement acceptance, public upload, repository visibility change or Devpost write has occurred. Optional webhook/Payouts verification is not part of the completed purchasing claim.

## How AI capabilities are used

Transformers.js runs the pinned q8 Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model on the coordinator's local Node server and produces 384-dimensional sentence embeddings. Cosine similarity supports a possible-duplicate explanation alongside receipt digest, amount, incident and time indicators. AI cannot approve, reject or execute a payment. Model assets must first be downloaded; disconnected field browsers preserve and transfer records rather than running the model on a phone. The 12-pair synthetic calibration produced TP5/FP0/FN1/TN6 on the same set used for threshold tuning; it is not held-out accuracy or a fraud probability. Details: [AI_MODEL.md](AI_MODEL.md).

## How Codex was used in the build process

Codex assisted implementation of the offline request/packet workflow, guarded Sandbox payment integration, local semantic review, audit validation, browser tests, compatibility-preserving rebrand and release documentation. It inspected source ancestry and dependency/model provenance and prepared the captioned application demo. Existing verification logs record execution of the app's unit/browser checks and real local inference. Genuine purchase approvals came from the actual user and genuine Sandbox checkout; Codex did not supply human financial decisions. This finalization continues the existing build without rebuilding the app or presenting old checks as new runs.

## Testing and judge access

Use the source-install path in [README.md](../README.md), Node.js 24+, npm, Python 3 for the one-time pinned model download, and Chromium. Configure a local coordinator passphrase and optional Sandbox-only PayPal credentials; no credentials are included in the submission. Run the production build locally so the service worker is active. Preserve a fictional request offline, reload, export RL1 packets and import into a second offline browser. Reconnect explicitly, upload for review, run local semantic review and inspect supporting indicators. A new Sandbox transaction requires an actual human REVIEW, AUTHORIZE, genuine buyer approval and separate CAPTURE; order creation alone is unpaid. Do not repeat the completed reference purchase. Validate the supplied seven-event export with `npm run audit:validate -- docs/evidence/paypal-sandbox-audit.json`. Inspect known limitations before testing callbacks or reimbursement transfer.

The audit CLI now validates the actual `events` array in an export envelope or a raw event array, rejects invalid shapes and checks the chain independently of claimed metadata. A judge-command review exposed the prior unchecked-envelope path; four new targeted CLI checks passed (genuine envelope, raw array, tamper rejection, missing-events rejection). This narrow verification does not imply a repeated whole suite. [Targeted checks](evidence/release-audit-cli-green.log); [seven-event command output](evidence/release-audit-envelope-green.log).

## Screenshots and demo

Actual application screenshots with fictional data: [desktop](evidence/interface-1440.png), [mobile](evidence/interface-390.png), [local AI review](evidence/review-ai.png), [audit](evidence/audit.png). Existing screenshots show their original automated UI fixtures; they are not footage of the independent human financial approval. New genuine screenshots show the [settled PAID screen](evidence/payment-completed.png) with actual references and disabled financial operation controls, and the [seven-event purchase audit](evidence/audit-paypal-completed.png) with export matching SQLite. The private [MP4](demo/waylatch-engineering-preview.mp4) preserves nonfinancial product footage and shows newly recorded actual settled PAID UI and the genuine seven-event audit, followed by a clearly identified sanitized provider-evidence insert. [Recording verification](evidence/settled-demo-recording.json) confirms disabled create/capture controls, browser export matching SQLite and unchanged financial state. It does not claim that buyer checkout/capture was screen-recorded. [Demo script](DEMO_SCRIPT.md), [narration](demo/NARRATION.md), [video metadata](evidence/demo-video.json).

Devpost project/submission URL: **PENDING approved creation and final entry**. Exact custom field IDs, labels, required choices/files, registration relationship and account identity: **UNKNOWN from failed read tools**, never invented. The complete structured drafting outline is in [devpost-submission.md](../devpost-submission.md); the review packet is [submission/SUBMISSION_PACKAGE.md](submission/SUBMISSION_PACKAGE.md).

[Fresh webhook release diagnostic](WEBHOOK_RELEASE_STATUS.md) found zero Sandbox registrations and zero returned events; three unsigned/synthetic callbacks were rejected HTTP400 without changing the copied PAID record or seven-event audit. These rejection checks do not prove genuine signed delivery.
